title: kv-transient-residency-reclaimer-and-spill-fanout-coordinator
author: Carmen Ortiz
description: Motivation: Under mixed read/write workloads with multi-tenant KV usage we observed correlated spill events and eviction storms that inflate p99 latency and increase storage I/O. This PR introduces a coordinated approach to reduce fragmentation and smooth spill activity by (1) a transient residency reclaimer that marks short-lived page allocations as transient to enable low-cost reclamation without full eviction, (2) a consolidation-aware allocator heuristic that prefers contiguous page runs when tenant locality signals are present, and (3) a spill fanout coordinator that shards spill targets per-tenant and applies staggered backoff windows to avoid synchronous spikes. The changes also add light-weight batch-level eviction hints emitted by the continuous-batching layer so the scheduler can sequence batches to avoid eviction hot loops. Work items in this PR: initial transient residency bitmap and reclaim path; consolidation-aware first-fit-with-lookahead allocator; spill fanout coordinator with tenant pools and stagger windows; integration with serving scheduler to carry eviction hints across batching boundaries; unit/integration tests and a benchmark harness. Checklist: - Implement transient residency flags and reclaim API - Integrate allocator lookahead into page allocator - Add spill fanout coordination service and per-tenant pools - Emit eviction hints from continuous-batching runtime - Add unit tests, end-to-end integration, and perf benchmark - Update docs/eviction.md and add migration notes Caveats/notes: the design favors predictable p99 behavior over absolute throughput in degenerate cases. Rollout plan: feature flagged by kv.reclaimer.enabled and spill.coordinator.enabled, can be enabled per-cluster and per-tenant for safety. Related: ENG-6382 for follow-up telemetry and ENG-6421 for tenant quota tuning.

review_comments: Ethan Nguyen (2026-02-02): Can you clarify the invariants the transient residency bit maintains? How do we avoid promoting a page to transient repeatedly and starving long-lived objects?

Carmen Ortiz (2026-02-03): Answer: residency is set on allocation and cleared on two types of stable accesses. There is a low-cost access counter threshold (configurable) that promotes a page out of transient. Added comments and a test that verifies transient->stable promotion to avoid starvation.

Priya Shah (2026-02-05): The allocator lookahead could worsen allocation latency in worst-case fragmentation. Can we add a fast path that falls back to first-fit when lookahead exceeds a latency budget?

Carmen Ortiz (2026-02-06): Implemented a bounded-lookahead fast-path. If the lookahead loop exceeds configured microsecond budget, it falls back to the fast first-fit allocator. Microbench shows negligible cost for typical workloads.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-10): CI flake on macOS test; looks unrelated but please add a retry or widen timeout on the integration harness. Approved after CI green and minor doc updates.

Ethan Nguyen (2026-02-12): Approved. Observed ~15% p99 reduction in our stress cluster run and 22% lower spill I/O for heavy tenant churn. Suggest follow-up to expose tenant spill metrics in console (ENG-6382).
Priya Shah (2026-02-15): Minor nit on log verbosity for the spill coordinator; changed to debug. Approving now that CI is stable.

Feature gated by kv.reclaimer.enabled and spill.coordinator.enabled. No rollback observed during canary.
release_notes: Introduce transient residency reclaimer to reduce eviction amplification and fragmentation. Add consolidation-aware allocator to improve contiguous page allocation and reduce future fragmentation. Add spill fanout coordinator to shard spill I/O across tenant pools and apply staggered backoff to avoid synchronous spill storms. Integrates with continuous-batching to emit eviction hints for smarter scheduling. Default is behind feature flags; recommended rollout per-cluster with monitoring on kv.spill.* metrics.
